real_estate.homebuilder: About one in three local sellers cut their asking price this past month, and about as many have every month since March.
real_estate.commentary:
Sellers are meeting today's rates partway. In Fremont, Hayward, Newark and Union City, 105 of the 308 homes on the market at both our Sept. 24 and Oct. 24 MLS exports lowered their asking price in between, or 34.1%, and the typical cut was 3.8%. Newark sellers cut the most, 22 of 48; Hayward the least, 27 of 107.

It is not a one month blip. In every month since March, between 33.2% and 40.4% of the listings in those four cities have cut, against 16% to 28% last fall and winter. Board wide, across 14 cities, it was 34.2% this month.

Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average ended the week at 7.33% and the 15-year at 6.98%; it does not update on weekends. Freddie Mac's weekly average was 7.32% Thursday. The Fed meets Tuesday and Wednesday, its first meeting since raising its rate in September.

Locally, inventory held steady. The board wide table rose to 2,640 from 2,636, with 133 coming soon and 205 brand new. The five city ledger rose to 688 from 684: Milpitas to 102 from 95 and Hayward to 198 from 194, while Fremont slipped to 230 from 235, Newark to 91 from 92 and Union City to 67 from 68.

What this means for you: a typical cut is worth real money. On our five city median of $1,075,000 with 20% down, a 3.8% cut takes about $40,850 off the price and about $225 off the monthly principal and interest at 7.33%, roughly what a rate near 6.94% would do. If you are buying, ask about price before you shop for a lower rate; if you are selling, a third of your competition has already cut, so price for today's payment from day one.

• Board wide: 2,640 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 133 coming soon and 205 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 688 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 618 are on the market and 70 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 230 live, 182 active, 29 coming soon, 18 brand new and 1 back on market. The median on market list price is $1,300,000 at $796 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 36 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 198, Milpitas 102, Newark 91, Union City 67.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,075,000 at $666 a square foot. 291 homes are priced under a million, and 176 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Friday, October 23 at the closing bell. For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.47%, the Nasdaq 0.71%, and the Dow rose 0.41%.
stocks.news:
Oil set the tone Friday. The Dow fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, as Brent climbed, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.52% and the Nasdaq 0.21% after Thursday's tech selloff.

American Express fell 3.68% even after record third quarter revenue of $20.1 billion, up 9%, adjusted earnings of $4.68 a share, up 13%, and a raised full year forecast; the quarter carried a $336 million restructuring charge. Next week brings the Fed and more big tech earnings, so enjoy the intermission.

economy.note: Levels are Friday, October 23: the 10-Year is Treasury's close, gold and silver are COMEX December settlements, and Brent is the ICE December settlement.
economy.commentary:
Oil kept climbing. Brent settled up 3.14% at $116.72 Friday on renewed Middle East tensions, its highest settlement since April 29, and gained 6.2% for the week from $109.86.

Bonds gave a little back. The 10-Year closed at 5.00%, up 0.04 point on the day but down 0.09 for the week. Gold settled down 1.29% at $4,007.90 and silver down 1.92% at $53.95, leaving gold $7.90 above $4,000, close enough that traders will be watching it Monday.

crypto.commentary: Crypto slipped into the weekend. Bitcoin is down 1.07% over 24 hours near $80,500, Ether is down 2.24% and XRP is down 1.13%, live from CoinGecko at 1:31 PM PT. Bitcoin is holding above $80,000, which these days passes for a quiet Saturday.
